title: Hybrid windowed coalescer for mixed-sequence workloads (continuous batching + KV reservation)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a hybrid windowed coalescer (HWC) to improve end-to-end token throughput and tail latency for mixed prompt/response length workloads. HWC combines an entropy-based short-window coalescer for low-latency short prompts with an opportunistic long-window consolidator that absorbs long-response requests for GPU memory packing and KV reservation. The feature integrates with the KV cache watermarking system and GPU slab-aware allocator to reduce memory fragmentation and unnecessary evictions.
motivation: Observed production workloads show highly skewed request length distributions (many short prompts interleaved with fewer very long responses). Existing continuous batcher either favors latency (thin windows) or throughput (thicker windows), leading to either wasted GPU cycles or long tail latencies and repeated KV evictions. HWC aims to adaptively split the request stream into short-latency lanes and throughput lanes while coordinating KV reservation and GPU slab packing to preserve SLOs and reduce unit cost.
success_metrics: p50 token latency <= baseline+5% for short prompts
p99 request latency reduced by >= 15% for mixed workloads
GPU memory fragmentation (free slab ratio) reduced by >= 20% during long-response bursts
KV eviction rate down by >= 30% for customers with mixed-length dialogs
tokens/sec per GPU increased by >= 8% on representative benchmarks
acceptance_criteria: HWC can be toggled per runtime via runtime config flag
Automated experiments show improved metrics on benchmark harness (see links)
No regression on existing latency-sensitive routes (canary tests passed)
Graceful fallback to current continuous-batcher when KV pressure > critical watermark
Documentation and console controls added for lane thresholds and KV reservation parameters
technical_design: HWC has three main components: (1) entropy estimator that computes a lightweight sequence-length and token-variance score per request to classify into lanes; (2) a dual-window coalescer: a fast-pass window (5-15ms) for low-entropy/short requests and a slow-pass window (20-80ms) for high-entropy/longer responses; (3) KV reservation & GPU packer that reserves a soft KV slab per slow-pass batch and requests GPU slab compaction when cross-batch packing improves utilization. The scheduler exposes per-route knobs: short_window_ms, long_window_ms, entropy_threshold, kv_soft_reserve_tokens, and slab_pack_aggressiveness. Watermarking: two thresholds (soft, critical) trigger different behaviors: soft watermark starts early eviction but prefers reservation for in-flight slow-pass batches; critical watermark disables slow-pass and forces short-pass only.
design_tradeoffs_decisions: Use entropy estimator instead of strict token-count heuristics to better handle variable response lengths in streaming chat use-cases.
Short-window upper bound chosen as 15ms to maintain perceived interactivity; measured regression risk and kept conservative to avoid user-facing latency.

KV soft reservation is optimistic (pre-allocate logical tokens) rather than hard allocation to avoid blocking high-throughput lanes; this reduces worst-case reservation overhead but requires robust early-release logic.
GPU slab compaction may increase CPU orchestration overhead; we bias aggressiveness toward customer tiers with higher unit-cost sensitivity.
Fallback logic prioritizes availability over throughput: on critical memory pressure we revert to existing batching behavior to avoid OOMs.
rollout_plan: Feature branch merged behind feature flag (runtime.hwc.enabled)
Unit + integration tests in CI covering lane classification edge cases
Canary on internal dev cluster with synthetic mixed-length traffic
Gradual rollout to 5% production region traffic for non-SLA routes
Monitor metrics for 48 hours; if no regressions, expand to 25% and then 100% for candidate routes
Expose per-customer override and opt-out in Console until feature matures
testing_plan: Synthetic harness: replay of mixed-dialog traces (internal dataset) against baseline and HWC; compare p50/p95/p99 latencies and KV eviction traces
Chaos tests: force KV cache pressure and ensure HWC disables slow-pass correctly
GPU memory profiling: measure slab fragmentation with and without slab compaction
A/B tests on a sampled set of accounts with telemetry for perceived latency and cost metrics
Load test: peak QPS with long-response bursts to verify no increase in error-rate or OOMs
progress_updates: 2026-03-11: Spike complete — implemented prototype entropy estimator and dual-window coalescer in experimental branch. Microbenchmarks show 6% tokens/sec improvement on mixed synthetic trace.

2026-03-12: Review with runtime team — agreed to add soft KV reservation semantics and two-watermark policy. Action: add early-release token logic to reduce reservation tail impact. (Reviewed by Maya Chen)

2026-03-13: Integration work started to surface slab_pack_aggressiveness via existing GPU allocator hooks. Discovered allocator API limitation: no current fast-count of contiguous free slabs, added allocator enhancement ticket ENG-88399.
2026-03-14: Canary config drafted and documented; created PR #1423 for coalescer and PR #1425 for KV reservation logic. Preparing CI integration tests. (Assigning QA for canary validations)
